title: Best Nightstands 2026: 5 Bedside Tables for Every Style
description: The best nightstands of 2026 — West Elm, CB2, IKEA, Pottery Barn, and Wayfair compared on storage, proportions, and how they hold up nightly.
lede: The nightstand gets used twice every day at minimum and ignored completely during room cleaning. It needs to hold a lamp, your phone (charging), a glass of water, and a book without looking cluttered. It needs a drawer deep enough to be useful and legs that don't snag a vacuum cleaner. These five cover the range from CB2's acrylic-framed modern piece to IKEA's classic Hemnes — which has been in production so long it's practically furniture vernacular.
methodology: Each nightstand was assessed on drawer depth and capacity, surface area for lamp and everyday items, height relative to standard mattress heights, stability under the weight of a lamp, and construction quality at the price point. We did not test these products ourselves.

sections.heading: What to Look for in a Nightstand
paragraphs: Nightstands are functional first — they need to hold what you reach for in the dark without things falling off. Dimensions and storage configuration matter more than aesthetics in this category.

subsections.heading: Height Relative to Your Mattress
paragraphs: The nightstand surface should be within 2-3 inches of your mattress top — ideally just above it. For a standard 25-inch platform bed or box spring setup, a 26-28 inch tall nightstand is correct. For a raised mattress on a high frame, you may need a taller piece (28-32 inches). For a low-profile platform frame with a thick mattress topping out at 24 inches, a 24-26 inch nightstand works. Measure your mattress height before ordering.

subsections.heading: Surface Area and Organization
paragraphs: A nightstand surface needs to hold a lamp, a glass of water, and your phone. That's roughly 15x18 inches of working area. A nightstand that's too small — under 14 inches square — means items constantly fall off. Slightly larger is always better. A built-in USB or wireless charging port eliminates the cable on the surface, which is worth paying for if it's available.

subsections.heading: Drawer Size and Depth
paragraphs: A shallow drawer (under 3 inches deep) is nearly useless — it holds reading glasses and lip balm but nothing else. A drawer with 5-6 inches of interior depth holds a book, a phone charger coiled up, some medication, and other bedside essentials. Two drawers are better than one if you share the bed. Check the drawer clearance before ordering — a drawer that hits the bed frame won't open fully.

subsections.heading: Stability Under Lamp Weight
paragraphs: A nightstand needs to hold a lamp without tipping when the lamp is bumped or the shade is adjusted. A wide, heavy base is more stable than a thin-legged piece. Stone or marble tops add natural stability. Check the leg-to-top ratio: a very small base with a relatively large top is a tipping risk, especially with a heavy ceramic lamp.

sections.heading: How These Five Stack Up
paragraphs: CB2's Acrylic Frame nightstand is the most visually distinctive in the group — the transparent acrylic legs create a floating effect that works particularly well in small bedrooms where visual weight matters. West Elm's Modern Mixed Material nightstand combines a marble or concrete top with a wood drawer — a material combination that bridges multiple design aesthetics.

IKEA's Hemnes is the predictable recommendation for budget nightstands, and it remains correct. Solid pine, a large drawer, and a lower shelf give it more storage than any comparable piece at the price. Pottery Barn's Sausalito is the storage-forward choice for people who accumulate bedside items. Wayfair's Mercury Row piece is the budget alternative with a designed appearance that doesn't telegraph its price.

sections.heading: Bottom Line
paragraphs: West Elm Mixed Material for a modern bedroom where materials mixing is part of the design language. CB2 Acrylic for a contemporary bedroom that needs visual lightness. IKEA Hemnes for the most storage at the best price. Pottery Barn Sausalito for a traditional bedroom with heavy storage needs. Wayfair Mercury Row when budget is the priority but you want something that looks like it cost more.

faqs.q: What height should a nightstand be?
faqs.a: A nightstand should be within 2-3 inches of your mattress top height. Measure from the floor to the top of your mattress (including any mattress topper) — that's your target nightstand height. For most platform beds with a 12-inch mattress, the total height is 22-25 inches, making a 24-26 inch nightstand ideal. For raised bed frames with box springs, the mattress top may be 28-32 inches, requiring a taller nightstand.

No — matching nightstands on both sides of the bed is a traditional approach but not a rule. Mixed nightstands (different heights, styles, or materials) can look intentional and design-forward if there's a connecting element, such as matching lamps or a shared color in both pieces. The main practical consideration is that both nightstands should be roughly the same height as the mattress surface.

faqs.q: How big should a nightstand surface be?
faqs.a: A working nightstand surface needs to hold a lamp, phone, glass of water, and at least one book. That requires roughly 15x18 inches of clear surface area. Most nightstands range from 18x18 to 24x18 inches — anything in that range works. Below 14x14 inches is too small for practical daily use without constant risk of items falling off.

faqs.q: Should nightstands have legs or sit on the floor?
faqs.a: Nightstands with legs allow easier cleaning underneath and create a visually lighter look. Nightstands that sit flat on the floor are more stable and may have more internal storage volume. For small bedrooms, legs create the impression of more floor space. For rooms with long-haired pets, a leg-free base that prevents dust from accumulating is slightly easier to maintain around.

faqs.q: What's a good nightstand for a very small bedroom?
faqs.a: In a small bedroom, a nightstand with a narrow footprint (14-16 inches deep) and visual lightness is important. Options include wall-mounted floating shelves, CB2's acrylic-legged pieces that don't add visual weight, or a small stool repurposed as a nightstand. Avoid tall, bulky nightstands with solid sides in a small bedroom — they make the space feel enclosed.

products.review: West Elm's Modern Mixed nightstand pairs a marble or concrete top with a walnut-finished wood drawer unit — the material contrast is the design point, and it works consistently across multiple bedroom aesthetics from Scandinavian to mid-century. The single drawer is properly sized at 5 inches deep. The top surface is 21x16 inches, which comfortably holds a lamp and bedside items without crowding. The metal frame connecting the marble top to the wood base is a clean design detail. West Elm's construction quality at this price tier is reliable — no flex in the frame, drawer glides smoothly after breaking in.
pros: Marble or concrete top paired with wood drawer creates genuine material interest
21x16 inch surface provides ample room for lamp and daily items
Drawer is properly sized at 5 inches deep
cons: Marble top option adds weight — difficult to move alone
Single drawer only — limited storage for nightstand essentials

products.review: CB2's acrylic frame nightstand uses a transparent leg frame that creates the impression of a floating surface — the visual weight is dramatically reduced compared to conventional wood or metal nightstands. This matters in small bedrooms where every visual element adds to the sense of crowding. The acrylic polishes clean and is resistant to light scratching at this thickness. The single drawer and top shelf provide adequate storage for most bedside configurations. The design looks contemporary and considered rather than budget-driven. For a small urban bedroom or a secondary bedroom where visual space matters, this is the most effective choice.
pros: Transparent acrylic legs create visual lightness — ideal for small rooms
Acrylic surface cleans easily and resists light scratches
Modern floating appearance is distinctive at this price
cons: Acrylic can yellow slightly over years under direct sunlight
Less storage volume than wood alternatives at a comparable price

products.review: IKEA's Hemnes nightstand is the budget recommendation that keeps being correct year after year. The solid pine construction is genuinely more durable than MDF alternatives at the same price. One large drawer (6 inches deep) and a lower shelf give it more storage than any comparable piece under $200. Available in painted white or black-brown — both work in most bedroom contexts. The drawer handle is a simple round pull. No USB or wireless charging integration, which is the main functional gap compared to contemporary alternatives. But for pure storage value and solid construction at this price, Hemnes remains the standard.
pros: Solid pine construction is more durable than MDF at same price tier
Large 6-inch deep drawer plus open lower shelf for maximum storage
Proven design in continuous IKEA production
cons: No built-in charging integration — separate cable management required
Painted finish chips at edges with regular contact over time

products.review: Pottery Barn's Sausalito is built for the bedroom that accumulates things — two drawers, a lower shelf, and a wide surface area of 22x17 inches means it can hold everything you reach for at night without crowding. The construction is solid: kiln-dried hardwood with dovetail drawer joints. Available in multiple wood finishes with matching hardware. The traditional paneled design suits period homes and classic bedrooms. For couples sharing storage where the nightstand is a primary organizational piece, the double drawer configuration is the most practical choice in this group.
pros: Two drawers plus lower shelf provide the most storage in this group
Kiln-dried hardwood with dovetail drawer construction is built to last
Wide 22x17 inch surface handles lamp plus multiple bedside items
cons: Traditional paneled design limits appeal in modern or minimal rooms
Higher price than comparable storage pieces at other retailers

products.review: Wayfair's Mercury Row nightstand does a convincing job of looking like a more expensive piece — the metal hairpin legs and wood top combination reads as intentional mid-century styling rather than flat-pack. The single drawer is adequately sized and the surface area is correct for a lamp and phone. The construction is lighter than Pottery Barn or West Elm, but for a guest bedroom or rental situation, it holds up fine under moderate use. The price makes it accessible for people furnishing a bedroom on a limited budget who don't want something that looks obviously cheap.
pros: Hairpin leg and wood top combination reads as designed, not budget
Adequate drawer size for typical nightstand storage needs
Very accessible price for the visual quality
cons: Lighter construction — not suitable for heavy daily use over many years
Hairpin legs can wobble slightly if not fully tightened during assembly

pinDescription: Five nightstands compared from CB2's floating acrylic piece to IKEA's storage-loaded Hemnes. Heights, drawer depths, and which is right for your bedroom.
